extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants and research teams preparing human subjects sections (PIs, study staff, IRB coordinators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and required elements for the Protection of Human Subjects, Data Safety and Monitoring, Inclusion, Recruitment, Consent, and confidentiality sections of an NIH grant application for studies involving caregivers and clinicians. Focused on operational procedures, risk mitigation, and IRB-related requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRB approval and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval to conduct this human subjects research will be sought from the Weill Cornell Medicine (WCM) Clinical Study Evaluation Committee (CSEC) and Institutional Review Board (IRB) and from Visiting Nurse Service of New York (VNSNY) IRB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multi-site and using same protocol at more than one domestic site, describe single IRB plan. The protocol and results will be reviewed annually by the WCM IRB. Report adverse events to relevant IRB(s) and/or federal agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written informed consent required
rubrics_metrics.description: All caregiver and clinician participants will be required to provide written informed consent before being enrolled in the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informed consent will be conducted by study personnel trained in consent procedures, who will review study procedures in detail and allow participant questions. Participants will be informed of rights including voluntary participation and ability to withdraw at any time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent form content (HIPAA/PHI and contacts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Per requirements of the WCM IRB and VNSNY IRB, the informed consent form will contain a section dedicated to explaining what constitutes protected health information and how this information remains confidential per HIPAA guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form will provide contact information for PI (Dr. Luth), the relevant IRB(s), and the Privacy Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent for audio-recording and use of aliases
rubrics_metrics.description: All interview and training and tool development participants will be asked to confirm that they consent for discussions to be audio-recorded and that they may use an alias during the discussion to further protect confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants will still be allowed to participate in the study even if they do not agree to be recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow participation without recording
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants will be allowed to take part in the study even if they do not agree to be audio-recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is explicitly stated for interviews, focus groups, and think-aloud exercises; non-consent to recording does not exclude participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of electronic medical records limited to identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Solely for the purpose of identifying potentially eligible family caregivers, data pertaining to patients’ age, ethnicity, functional and cognitive status, or date of most recent doctor visit or upcoming appointment (Aim 1), and caregiver contact information will be obtained through a review of WMC electronic medical records (Aim 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information will not be used or analyzed elsewhere in the study beyond identifying participation eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection of basic contact/identifying information for recruitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect basic identifying information for all participants who are identified as potentially eligible or who indicate interest, including name, address, phone number, and email so that we can contact them, determine eligibility, and schedule consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information obtained from VNSNY will be shared through WCM’s secure file transfer system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding and storage of participant identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign individuals enrolled in the study a unique identifier number to which data collected will be linked. A document linking study identifier numbers to identifying information will be stored in a single document on a secure WCM server in a folder that can only be accessed by credentialed study personnel on password-protected computers stored in locked offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only study personnel will have access to study files. All study data will be coded with unique participant identification numbers; participant names and other identifying information will not be recorded on study materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure storage of electronic and paper data
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic and digital data will be stored on a secure server on a password-protected computer at WCM. All written material (paper transcripts of interviews, and other recordings containing participant identifiers) will be stored in a locked file cabinet in a locked office at WCM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coded participant data may also be stored on a password protected RedCap account. Only credentialed study personnel have access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audio file transcription and destruction
rubrics_metrics.description: With participant consent, all interviews/focus groups will be audio-recorded and transcribed. As soon as the audio-files are transcribed, they will be destroyed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants who decline recording are still allowed to participate; destruction occurs after transcription to protect privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits of confidentiality and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidentiality may be suspended in the event of an emergency (e.g., detection of abuse, suicidal ideation or psychological distress). Participants will be informed of the limits of confidentiality during the consent process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such events, a social worker/psychiatrist will be consulted and appropriate reporting (e.g., to PCP or practice social worker) will occur; participants are provided with PI contact information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling distress and potential harm discovered in interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Caregivers may find interview questions upsetting and may experience emotional distress. Participants who exhibit distress will be encouraged to speak with their primary care physician or to call the Eldercare Locator hotline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In more severe or acute cases, a social worker (Marlena Palombo, MSW) and/or psychiatrist (Robert Abrams, MD) will be consulted and the participant will be referred to the appropriate level of care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting suspected abuse
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a rare possibility of uncovering abuse within a patient-caregiver relationship. We will report these cases directly to the patient’s primary care physician and/or to the practice social worker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such reporting may require suspension of confidentiality as described above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data safety procedures and access controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Study data will be stored on a secure server in a folder that can only be accessed by credentialed study personnel on a password-protected computer at WCM. A separate file linking names and study ID numbers will also be password-protected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only study personnel will have access to study files; electronic sharing between sites should use secure file transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and safety monitoring activities and schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Tracking forms will be developed to document when the review of study data occurs. Dr. Luth will review all consent forms as they are received. Participant recruitment and enrollment will be recorded by the study RA who will generate a weekly report for Dr. Luth. Dr. Luth will review self-report measures for completeness and accuracy of entry into RedCap on a weekly basis. All data will be reviewed semi-annually by Dr. Luth and her mentorship team; the study protocol and results will be reviewed annually by the WCM IRB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document the frequency and responsible persons for reviews and reporting; maintain logs/reports to demonstrate ongoing monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse event detection and reporting timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The study RA or PI may become aware of adverse events through participant self-report or interactions. Dr. Luth will report any adverse events with caregiver or clinician participants to the WCM IRB and/or federal agencies and with VNSNY clinician interview participants to the VNSNY IRB and/or federal agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All adverse events noted by study personnel will be discussed with Dr. Luth and will be reported within 24 hours of discovery to the IRB(s). Discuss safety concerns, adverse events, participant complaints, and protocol violations with the full research team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel training requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All study personnel will have completed the NIH required training in participation and conduct of studies involving human subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study personnel obtaining consent will be trained in consent procedures; ensure documentation of trainings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of women and minorities policy
rubrics_metrics.description: No participants will be excluded on the basis of their gender or race/ethnicity. The study will sample equal numbers of African-American and white family caregivers by design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides projected gender and racial composition estimates for participants and clinicians (e.g., expect total sample ~70-80% female). Include Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children documentation (S2 Inclusion...).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion (exclusion) of children
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals under 18 years of age will not be included in this research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: study focuses on family and professional caregiving for patients with dementia; clinician training requirements necessitate clinicians be over 18.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment sites and enrollment targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Data will be collected from consenting family caregivers and clinicians recruited from multiple recruitment sites in New York City, including two adult primary care clinics (at WCM), a large hospice provider (VNSNY), and with support of community partner CaringKind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables provide anticipated enrollment across recruitment sites and aims; sample sizes account for overlap (e.g., interview participants may also participate in stakeholder feedback).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment and retention strategies to minimize burden
rubrics_metrics.description: To minimize burden on clinician participants, training and feedback sessions will be conducted during regular team meetings. To minimize burden on family caregivers, tool feedback sessions will be scheduled at participants’ convenience and, whenever feasible, at location of their choosing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feasibility testing will use two VNSNY hospice teams (~10 clinicians each) and recruit 20 FCG (10 African American, 10 white) and 10 clinicians to provide feedback. One-time encounters are used to limit retention concerns. Plan to disseminate findings to participants who request them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessments and types of data collected
rubrics_metrics.description: Baseline assessments include self-reported demographic information (age, gender, race, ethnicity, marital status). Family caregivers provide information about religious beliefs and experiences with discrimination. Family caregivers and clinicians complete baseline assessments of dementia knowledge and strategies; caregivers complete caregiver burden; clinicians complete implicit bias assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify time frames and measurement instruments in protocol; ensure data entry completeness and accuracy in RedCap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol synopsis requirements (design, masking, allocation, outcomes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Protocol synopsis must describe study design: primary purpose, interventions (type/name/description), study phase (is this an NIH-defined Phase III Clinical Trial?), intervention model, masking (participant, care provider, investigator, outcomes assessor), allocation, outcome measures (type/name/time frame/brief description), statistical design and power, subject participation duration, FDA-regulated intervention questions, and dissemination plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the Protocol Synopsis section with explicit answers for trial registration and regulatory commitments (e.g., ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier if applicable).
